correctness.rationale: Graph-automorphism averaging is legal because P↦||P−J||₂ is convex and invariant. The exact Fourier modes give largest nontrivial eigenvalue 1−min_j a_jc_j and smallest 1−Σa_jL_j, hence minmax lower bound max(1−t,Et−1) for t≤1/H. Equality sets a_j=τ/c_j, with uniqueness among invariant kernels. For arbitrary P attaining the same SLEM, each first coordinate Fourier mode f_j saturates the PSD upper norm inequality and must be an eigenvector; its real and imaginary vertexwise components force w_j^+=w_j^−=τ/c_j and row-sums fix the diagonal. The last inequality Σ_j (4−L_j)/c_j <1 reduces exactly to the claimed odd-factor threshold including 3 C3 boundary. Correct at d=1 and nonbipartite/bipartite boundaries.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-family mixing optimization including unrestricted nonhomogeneous kernels, with a surprising holding/no-holding frontier depending only on odd cycle-factor counts rather than individual lengths; a useful sharp design rule for finite toroidal random walks.

final_claim: For every finite Cartesian product of cycles of length n_j≥3, the unique globally optimal symmetric stochastic nearest-neighbor/self-loop transition kernel, with no invariance imposed a priori, has edge weights τ/c_j and hold 1−τH, τ=min{2/(E+1),1/H} with H=Σ2/c_j,E=ΣL_j/c_j. Positive holding occurs exactly with ≤2 odd factors or 3 odd factors not all triangular; the optimal SLEM is 1−τ.
limitations: n_j≥3, d≥1, graph edges and optional self-loops only.
Symmetric kernels and SLEM, not nonreversible kernels or finite-time total-variation optimality.
